# Community Rule Column 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QS (Cave 1), Col. 10 | **Condition:** complete

---

**10:1** When day and night arrive, I will enter into God's covenant; when evening departs and morning comes, I will recite His laws;

**10:2** and as long as they endure, I will hold firm to my limits and never turn back. I accept His judgment even for my own failures,

**10:3** and my sins remain always before my eyes like an inscription cut in stone. To God I will say, "You are my Righteousness,"

**10:4** and to the Most High, "You are the foundation of my good, the wellspring of all I know, the fountain of what is holy,

**10:5** the summit of glory, the Almighty whose splendor lasts forever." I will embrace whatever He teaches me and accept however He judges me.

**10:6** When light begins its reign across the sky, and when it returns to its resting place;

**10:7** when the watches of darkness begin, as He opens their treasury and pours them out above,

**10:8** and as they cycle round and are gathered back before the light; when the heavenly lights shine out

**10:9** from their sacred dwelling and return to their place of splendor —

**10:10** when the appointed seasons come according to the days of the month, each completing its turn

**10:11** from one to the next; when they renew themselves — a magnificent day, most sacred of all,

**10:12** a sign that His eternal mercy is being revealed; at the start

**10:13** of every season yet to come; at the beginning of each month in its proper time,

**10:14** and each holy festival in its rightful order, as a remembrance kept in its season.

**10:15** With words of praise I will bless Him, following a decree

**10:16** written for all time; at the turning of each year and through the cycle of its seasons,

**10:17** when the pattern of their order reaches completion — every day fulfilling its purpose:

**10:18** harvest yielding to summer heat, planting time yielding to fresh green shoots,

**10:19** years measured out in their sabbatical weeks; and at the start of each week of years,

**10:20** a season of freedom and release. For as long as I live, there is a decree inscribed

**10:21** upon my tongue — it is the fruit of praise, the offering of my lips.

**10:22** I will sing with understanding, and every melody I make will honor God;

**10:23** my lyre and harp will serve His sacred purpose, and the song on my lips

**10:24** I will lift up to His perfect standard. When day and night

**10:25** arrive, I will enter God's covenant, and when evening departs and morning

**10:26** comes, I will recite His laws — and within them I will mark out my boundaries.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The Hymn of the Instructor is one of the most beautiful liturgical compositions from Qumran. The maskil weaves worship into every rhythm of creation — the alternation of day and night, the lunar months, the agricultural calendar, and the great sabbatical cycles. The passage breathes with cosmic reverence, declaring that every moment of time is an occasion for praise. The inclusio (10:1 and 10:24-26) frames the entire passage as a single sustained act of covenantal devotion.*
